SPORT_COMPLETENESS_AUDIT_02 - audit of the SPORTING estate of the UK major-event venue census (census baseline 642 venues). Scope covered: rugby union, rugby league, cricket, horse racing, motorsport, and a systematic-gap spot-audit of football. Indoor arenas, greyhound, ice hockey, basketball, athletics and tennis were OUT OF SCOPE for this workstream (handled separately) and were deliberately not worked on.

THIS FILE CONTAINS 92 RECORDS: 80 NEW VENUES and 12 CORRECTION RECORDS. New venues break down as 36 rugby union grounds, 22 cricket grounds, 9 motorsport venues (5 circuits + 4 speed hillclimbs), 7 rugby league grounds and 6 football stadiums. 0 racecourses were added - horse racing was audited and found genuinely complete. Every correction record deliberately reuses the census's EXACT existing canonical_name and city so it reconciles onto the record it corrects, and asserts no capacity unless it is correcting one.

=== PER-SPORT AUTHORITATIVE POPULATIONS CHECKED, AND VERDICTS ===

1) HORSE RACING - VERDICT: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE. Population checked: the operating Great Britain racecourse estate (via greatbritishracing.com/racecourses/, which reports 59 results, and the Wikipedia List of British racecourses, which states 59 operating in Great Britain as of 17 September 2026), plus Northern Ireland's two courses, plus the two operator portfolios (thejockeyclub.co.uk lists 14 racecourses; arenaracingcompany.co.uk/racing/horse-racing/our-racecourses lists 16). Expected population 59 GB + 2 NI = 61. Census had 61. ADDED 0. The census's 59 GB courses were diffed name-by-name against the authoritative 59 and match EXACTLY. Both operator attributions also reconcile exactly: the census's 14 Jockey Club courses and 16 ARC courses match the operators' own published portfolios. NO CLOSED COURSE IS WRONGLY RETAINED - Folkestone (last raced 18 December 2012) and Towcester (closed 2018) are both correctly absent, and Hereford, which closed in 2012 and reopened in 2016, is correctly present as OPERATIONAL. This sport needed correction in neither direction.

2) MOTORSPORT - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED. Population checked: the Motorsport UK / operator-portfolio permanent circuit estate (msv.com, barc.net/about/, motorsportuk.org, motorsportni.org). EXPECTED_POPULATION_UNKNOWN - no governing body publishes a definitive count of licensed permanent circuits with public spectator calendars. Census had 14. ADDED 9 (5 circuits: Mallory Park, Lydden Hill, Kirkistown, Three Sisters, Crail Raceway; plus 4 speed hillclimbs: Shelsley Walsh, Prescott, Harewood, Gurston Down). The most material gap is KIRKISTOWN - the census contained NO Northern Irish motorsport circuit at all. Rockingham Motor Speedway (closed 24 November 2018) and Arena Essex/Lakeside (last meeting 4 November 2018) were verified closed and are correctly ABSENT from the census, so no closed circuit is wrongly retained. Bedford Autodrome was examined and deliberately EXCLUDED: MSV operate it, but its own site shows it is a PalmerSport corporate/track-day venue "with no requirement for crowd-protecting safety barriers", i.e. not a public spectator race facility. Blyton Park and Teesside Autodrome were excluded on the same basis.

3) RUGBY UNION - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED, and the census was a SEASON OUT OF DATE. Populations checked: PREM Rugby (premrugby.com/clubs/, 10 clubs); Champ Rugby, English tier 2 (the RFU-operated champrugby.com plus the 2026-27 Champ Rugby teams-and-stadia table, 14 clubs); the URC's UK clubs; and the Welsh and Scottish club estates via the two unions' own shared fixture platforms (my.wru.wales/fixtures-results and fixtures.scottishrugby.org/club-rugby). Census had 40 RUGBY_STADIUM records (covering both codes). ADDED 36 rugby union venues - 13 in England (Champ Rugby), 1 PREM Rugby, 13 in Wales and 9 in Scotland. Findings: (a) PREM Rugby - exactly ONE gap, StoneX Stadium (Saracens); the other nine clubs' grounds were all present, several under FOOTBALL_STADIUM (Ashton Gate, Principality). (b) URC - COMPLETE; all seven UK clubs' grounds present. (c) Champ Rugby - 10 of 14 grounds missing. CRITICAL: the obvious source (the 2025-26 season table) is STALE - Cambridge and London Scottish have been relegated out, and Blackheath (Well Hall) and Rotherham Titans (Clifton Lane) promoted in; Coventry's ground was renamed from Butts Park Arena to the Nick Newbold Stadium with effect from 21 March 2026. The 2026-27 table was used instead. (d) WALES - 11 major grounds >= 1,000 missing, including Newport Stadium, which a NAME COLLISION was hiding: it is Newport RFC's actual regular home since October 2021 and is a DIFFERENT venue from Rodney Parade, which the census already held. (e) SCOTLAND - 8 grounds missing, including The Greenyards (home of the Melrose Sevens) and Raeburn Place (site of the first rugby international, 27 March 1871).

4) RUGBY LEAGUE - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED. Population checked: superleague.co.uk/clubs (14 clubs, 12 UK after excluding Catalans Dragons and Toulouse Olympique) and the 2026 Betfred Championship (rugby-league.com plus the 2026 RFL Championship article). STRUCTURAL FINDING: RFL LEAGUE 1 NO LONGER EXISTS for 2026 - rugby-league.com states "Following confirmation of a merger of the Championship and League 1 competitions at the end of last season, 2026 will include 21 teams", reduced to 20 after Featherstone Rovers were removed following December 2025 administration. So the expected population is 12 UK Super League grounds + 20 Championship grounds. ADDED 7 grounds (Steel City Stadium, South Leeds Stadium, Morson Stadium, Stadiwm Eirias, Victoria Pleasure Grounds, Crow Trees Ground, Avery Fields). All 12 UK Super League grounds were already present.

5) CRICKET - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED, materially. Populations checked: the 18 first-class county headquarters; the county outground/festival estate via each county's own grounds pages (Kent, Surrey, Sussex, Middlesex, Lancashire, Derbyshire, Yorkshire, Gloucestershire, Worcestershire); Cricket Scotland and the Wikipedia list of cricket grounds in Scotland; and Cricket Ireland's international grounds. The census's 20 comprise all 18 first-class county HQs plus Stormont and The Grange - i.e. the HQ layer was complete but the ENTIRE non-HQ layer was missing. ADDED 22 cricket grounds. Highlights: North Marine Road Scarborough (the principal English outground), Arundel Castle (a genuine international venue with the richest outground calendar found anywhere in this audit), and AO FARINGTON - Lancashire CCC's purpose-built SECOND HOME, opened 2026 on a 250-year lease, which is the most significant new non-HQ cricket venue in the UK. Scotland went from 1 cricket ground to 5 (Mannofield Park Aberdeen is larger than The Grange by the cited figures); Northern Ireland from 1 to 4.

6) FOOTBALL (spot-audit for systematic gaps only - the long tail was deliberately NOT ground through) - VERDICT: the top tiers are NEARLY complete but contain one severe classification gap. Populations checked: Premier League (20), EFL Championship (24), League One (24), League Two (24), National League (24), SPFL Premiership/Championship/League One/League Two (12/10/10/10), Cymru Premier and NIFL Premiership (12). Census had 284 FOOTBALL_STADIUM records. ADDED 6 football stadiums, plus 6 football-side correction records (Coventry Building Society Arena, Keepmoat Stadium, York Street, Cae-y-Castell, Spotland, Plough Lane). Per-league: Premier League MISSING 1; EFL Championship, League One and League Two COMPLETE; National League MISSING 5 (Meadow Park Borehamwood, Hornchurch Stadium, The Lamb Ground, Grosvenor Vale, Woodside Road); Scottish Premiership and Championship COMPLETE; Scottish League One MISSING 1 (K-Park, East Kilbride); Scottish League Two MISSING 1 (Meadowbank Stadium); Cymru Premier COMPLETE; NIFL Premiership COMPLETE.
  - THE HEADLINE FOOTBALL FINDING: Coventry City were promoted to the Premier League for 2026-27, and the census holds the Coventry Building Society Arena ONLY as an EXHIBITION_CENTRE (with a second record for the indoor arena inside it). The 32,609-capacity stadium bowl is entirely absent from the census's football estate. This is a CLASSIFICATION gap, not a missing venue, which is why a football-stadium-list diff alone would report it as "present".
  - A CORRECTION TO THE TASK'S OWN PREMISE: the Cymru Premier is 16 clubs in 2026-27, not 12 - it expanded this season. Coverage is nonetheless complete (15 distinct grounds; Connah's Quay Nomads and Flint Town United share Cae-y-Castell).
  - DELIBERATE SUB-THRESHOLD EXCLUSION: K-Park Training Academy (East Kilbride, SPFL League One) is a genuine gap but its only cited capacity is 700, below this census's 1,000 threshold, so it is reported here and NOT added as a venue record.

=== VENUES FOUND WRONGLY RECORDED IN THE EXISTING CENSUS ===
Re-listed here as correction records using the census's EXACT existing canonical_name and city so they reconcile onto the same record:
 - DUPLICATE: "Keepmoat Stadium" (RUGBY_STADIUM, Doncaster) and "Club Doncaster Sports Village" (FOOTBALL_STADIUM, Doncaster) are the SAME physical stadium held twice under two names and two venue_types. The name is also two sponsor generations stale (Keepmoat 2006-2021, Eco-Power 2021-2026, Club Doncaster Sports Village from 2026) and the RUGBY_STADIUM classification is wrong - it is owned and operated by Doncaster Rovers F.C.
 - DUPLICATE CLUB ATTRIBUTION: "York Street" (Boston) is attributed to Boston United F.C., but the club moved to the Boston Community Stadium (opened December 2020), which the census ALSO holds attributed to the same club.
 - WRONG CITY AND WRONG PRIMARY CLUB: "Cae-y-Castell, at Flint" is recorded with city "Connah's Quay"; the ground is in Flint, and it is Flint Town United's home, with Connah's Quay Nomads a groundshare tenant. Both clubs are in the Cymru Premier, so one row silently covers two top-flight clubs.
 - NO LONGER A CRICKET VENUE: "St Helen's Rugby and Cricket Ground" (Swansea) - Glamorgan announced in July 2024 it would not return, and the final cricket match was played on 31 August 2025. Rugby use is unaffected.
 - SCRAPE ARTIFACT: "Milltown Park" (Warrenpoint) has the operator "Warrenpoint F.C.?action=edit&redlink=1" - a raw Wikipedia redlink query string. Two milder artifacts of the same scrape exist elsewhere and are reported but not separately recorded: "Airdrieonians F.C. (2002)" and "Everton F.C. (women)".
 - STALE SPONSOR NAMES (6 rugby league grounds, all confirmed against Sheffield Eagles' own 2026 fixture list): Craven Park Barrow -> Northern Competitions Stadium; Recreation Ground Whitehaven -> The Ortus Rec; Crown Flatt -> FLAIR Stadium; Derwent Park -> Fibrus Community Stadium; Spotland -> Crown Oil Arena; Plough Lane -> Cherry Red Records Stadium.
 - CLUB-NO-LONGER-THERE (venues remain valid; only the implied rugby league tenancy is stale, so these are reported not re-listed): Kingston Park (Newcastle Thunder left for Crow Trees Ground); Queensway Stadium Wrexham (North Wales Crusaders are at Stadiwm Eirias); Twickenham Stoop (London Broncos are at Plough Lane); Post Office Road Featherstone (Featherstone Rovers removed from the 2026 season).

=== SHARED OPERATOR/LEAGUE CALENDAR PLATFORMS FOUND (high value for collector reuse) ===
 - ARC (16 racecourses): https://www.<course>-racecourse.co.uk/whats-on/ - verified with dated meetings at Doncaster and Bath. Exceptions to the pattern: ffoslasracecourse.com, fontwellpark.co.uk, lingfieldpark.co.uk.
 - JOCKEY CLUB (14 racecourses): https://www.thejockeyclub.co.uk/<course>/events-tickets/ - verified with dated meetings at Cheltenham.
 - MOTORSPORT VISION (5 UK circuits in ONE feed): https://www.msv.com/calendar - verified with dated events. Each circuit domain serves the same group-wide calendar, e.g. https://www.cadwellpark.co.uk/calendar lists all MSV circuits. NOTE: /calendar works, /calendar/ 404s; Donington is donington-park.co.uk (hyphenated).
 - CHAMP RUGBY (all 14 clubs, RFU-operated): champrugby.com embeds an Oval-Hub widget resolving to a public JSON endpoint returning 188 matches for 2026/27 with stable matchId UUIDs, ISO-8601 UTC kickoffs AND venue names. The single highest-value artefact found; full call details are in the calendar_sources notes on every Champ Rugby venue here.
 - ANICC / NORTHERN IRELAND MOTORSPORT: https://www.motorsportni.org/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events - a public WordPress JSON REST API covering ALL NI motorsport venues. The cleanest acquisition path found in this audit. Use the API, not the HTML (/events/ times out; /venues/ 404s).
 - WRU (all Welsh club leagues): https://my.wru.wales/fixtures-results - JavaScript-rendered, and shows NO venue name in list view.
 - SCOTTISH RUGBY (200+ clubs, seasons to 2026/2027): https://fixtures.scottishrugby.org/club-rugby - stable per-competition URLs; also JavaScript-rendered with no venue name in list view.
 - BRITISH SPEEDWAY (all clubs, multi-stadium): https://britishspeedway.co.uk/calendar/2026-fixtures-results/ - verified with dated cross-club fixtures. Individual speedway club domains are largely dead or parked.
 - BARC: https://www.barc.net/events/ is an ORGANISER calendar spanning circuits BARC does not own (Silverstone, Brands Hatch, Goodwood, even Le Mans) - useful as a cross-check, dangerous if treated as a venue feed. NOTE barc.net fails TLS chain verification in some fetchers but serves correctly to curl.

=== EVIDENCE-QUALITY CAVEATS, STATED HONESTLY ===
 - SEASONAL TIMING: today is 2026-09-20. The 2026 rugby league season has FINISHED and the English cricket season is in its final week, so many first-party calendars legitimately show no forthcoming fixtures. Every such case is recorded events_currently_present:false with the reason stated - this reflects calendar timing, not an absent calendar, and these sources are worth re-checking in November/December 2026.
 - NO OFFICIAL CAPACITY EXISTS FOR WHOLE CLASSES OF VENUE. Established as a systematic finding, not an excuse: no county club or ECB page states a capacity for ANY non-headquarters cricket ground; no Champ Rugby club site states a capacity for any of the 13 grounds checked; and neither the WRU nor Scottish Rugby publishes ground capacities. Those capacities are therefore GRADE_C/LOW by necessity and must not be laundered into club-sourced facts.
 - HONEST NULLS: 25 records carry capacity_value null with capacity_confidence CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. 16 of those are new venues where no number could honestly be cited, and each carries documented scale facts instead: all 5 new circuits, all 4 hillclimbs, The Greenyards and Myreside (sources conflicting by more than an order of magnitude), The Lamb Ground, Crow Trees Ground, Avery Fields, AO Farington and College Ground Cheltenham. Two of those 16 (Crow Trees Ground, Avery Fields) carry an EXPLICIT REVIEWER WARNING that the 1,000 threshold is NOT established on cited evidence and that a reviewer may legitimately reject them. The other 9 nulls are correction records that deliberately assert no capacity so the census's existing figure is left untouched.
 - NO RECORD IN THIS FILE CARRIES A CAPACITY BELOW THE 1,000 THRESHOLD. Where a documented figure fell below it - K-Park Training Academy (700) and AO Farington's official 700 fixed seats - it is reported in prose or in additional_capacities and was NOT used as a principal capacity.
 - UNRESOLVED CONFLICTS RETAINED, NEVER AVERAGED: Scarborough 9,000 vs 11,500; Titwood 6,000 vs 5,000; AO Farington 700 official fixed seats vs 5,000 third-party; Stadiwm Eirias 6,080 vs 5,500; The Gnoll 6,000 vs 7,500; Talbot Athletic Ground 8,000 vs 10,000; Hornchurch 3,500 vs 3,000; Tamworth 4,000 vs 4,565; Meadowbank 1,320 vs 1,280; Ealing 5,388 vs 5,000; Bedwas 3,000 vs 2,000; The Greenyards 1,174 vs 16,024; Myreside 13,799 vs 5,500.
 - DATES NEVER INFERRED: Surrey's Guildford match-day guide names a fixture "Wednesday, 19 August" with NO YEAR, and Carmarthen Quins' site shows "Saturday 26 September" with no year. No year was inferred for either; both are recorded events_currently_present:false.
 - ONE DISCREPANCY DELIBERATELY NOT NORMALISED: Bedford Blues' own fixture list gives "Olney Field" as the venue for Ampthill's 21 Nov 2026 home match, where RFU league data gives "Dillingham Park" for all 13 Ampthill home matches.
 - A HIJACKED DOMAIN TO BLOCKLIST: neathrugby.co.uk is NOT Neath RFC - it now serves a rugby-betting content farm. The real site is neathrfc.com.

=== RESIDUAL GAPS NOT CLOSED (no completeness is claimed for these) ===
 - English rugby union tier 3 (National League 1) grounds were treated as outside "major Championship and representative venues" and were NOT enumerated. Cambridge (now "Ellgia Fields", a sponsor rename) and London Scottish drop into this tier for 2026-27 and are therefore not added here.
 - 13 cricket grounds qualify structurally but NO capacity could be established for any of them, so they were not admitted: Trafalgar Road Southport (Lancashire, active to 2026), Clifton Park York, Brunton Memorial Ground Radlett, Merchant Taylors' Northwood, Horsham, Forthill Dundee, Cambusdoon New Ground Ayr, Spytty Park Newport, Sedbergh School, Polo Farm Canterbury, Newclose (Isle of Wight), Castle Park Colchester, Wallace Park Lisburn.
 - 5 rugby union grounds staging Premiership/National-1 rugby have NO establishable capacity and were not admitted: Millbrae (Ayr - the current Scottish champions), Braidholm (GHA), Riverside Park (Jed-Forest), Lewis Lloyd Ground (Narberth), The Welfare Ground (Newbridge).
 - 3 Welsh grounds were left out as TOO SUSPECT to admit without a dedicated investigation: Abertillery Park (a 15,250 figure for a tier-3 club), Bargoed Park, Mount Pleasant Park Beddau.
 - THE SPEEDWAY STADIUM ESTATE IS NOT COVERED HERE. British Speedway's own 2026 club indexes give 6 SGB Premiership and 9 SGB Championship clubs, and several of their stadiums (e.g. Foxhall Ipswich, National Speedway Stadium Manchester, Shielfield Park Berwick) are absent from the census. It was left out deliberately because speedway stadiums overlap heavily with the greyhound-stadium estate being handled by a separate workstream, and duplicating it risked colliding records. IMPORTANT TRAP recorded for whoever takes it: owlertonstadium.co.uk is the GREYHOUND stadium's site and its /whats-on/ calendar is greyhound racing, not Sheffield Tigers speedway.
 - Motorsport items left unresolved: Shakespeare County Raceway's status (absent from 2026 drag listings but closure NOT evidenced - do not record it as closed); Bishopscourt Racing Circuit (its official domain now serves an unrelated store); Melbourne Raceway, Manston Raceway Park and Elvington (no resolvable official sites); Somerset Oak Tree Arena (redirect loop).
 - Sheffield Eagles' secondary home venue, The MEPS International Home of Football Stadium (Sheffield FC, Dronfield), has no establishable capacity and was not admitted.
 - Isle of Man TT / Mountain Course: explicitly dispositioned as OUT OF UK SCOPE - the Isle of Man is a Crown Dependency, not part of the UK, and the course is a closed-public-road circuit rather than a permanent one. Same reasoning excludes the NI road races (North West 200, Dundrod).
 - NOT AUDITED AT ALL, by instruction: indoor arenas, greyhound stadiums, ice hockey, basketball, athletics and tennis.

=== METHOD/TOOLING LIMITS ===
Every capacity, address, postcode and calendar claim in this file cites a URL that was actually fetched; where a fact could not be established it is recorded as null with the absence itself evidenced, rather than guessed. OpenStreetMap was NOT used for completeness anywhere. The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted partway through, after which enumeration relied on direct fetches of known governing-body, league and operator URLs; this limited discovery of venues for which no candidate URL was already held, and is the main reason the residual gaps above remain open.
